clue.text: Old Spice constituent once — a con almost

parts.note: Geri Halliwell, Ginger Spice, was a member of the Spice Girls until she left in 1998
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a con is a trick, a swindle

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned aftershave ingredient is dismissed as nearly a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Spice' reads as the aftershave brand, but Old is the definition and Spice points to the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is used, often rudely, to describe elderly people, so it stands for old.

clue.text: Let's go to Rock Junction? Piss off!

indicators.note: rock means shake, so the letters are rocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a T-junction gives the letter T

explanation.surface: A suggested trip to a place called Rock Junction meets a rude refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock Junction reads as a place name; Rock is the signal to rearrange and Junction gives a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rude exclamations telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Sweet arse-over-tip sailor's leaving the dance

indicators.note: leaving means those letters go out of the dessert's name

parts.note: a rum baba is a sweet, a syrup-soaked dessert

indicators.note: arse over tip means head over heels, so the sailor's two letters are turned upside down

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A sweet sailor tumbles head over heels and walks out of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Like a good preservative jar gets Melody pissed?

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
tight is slang for drunk, as is pissed in British English

explanation.surface: A jar of preserves somehow gets a woman called Melody drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Melody looks like a woman's name; it is a tune. Pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar used for preserving must be sealed so no air gets in, which is what airtight describes.

clue.text: A crafty makeover and stuck-up Brenda's sexually attractive

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck up means written upwards, so the cipher is reversed

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER; the 's stands for is
fit is British slang for sexually attractive

explanation.surface: The snooty Queen, after some artful cosmetic work, is declared sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: Crafty means 'for a craft': a refit is the overhaul of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is the renovation and re-equipping of a vessel, a makeover for a boat.

clue.text: Beaten with clothes on?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read playfully: clobber is British slang for clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented for the joke, hence the question mark: clobber means clothes, so clobbered could mean clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to hit them hard, so the past form means thrashed or beaten.

clue.text: Woman of diminished sex appeal featured in tabloid

indicators.note: featured in means one item is placed inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
diminished means shortened: sex appeal is cut down to its initials

explanation.surface: A woman who has lost her allure turns up in the gossip pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female given name, so it serves as an example of a woman.

clue.text: Climax, seeing Melinda's top doubly festooned with diamonds, say

indicators.note: festooned with means wrapped round by, so the card word surrounds the letters

parts.note: diamonds is one suit in a pack of cards

indicators.note: doubly means that letter is used twice
top means the first letter of the name in a down clue

parts.note: the name whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A celebrity gossip snippet about Melinda's top dripping with diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point or peak of something, its climax.

clue.text: Party whip first to grab Secretary for torture

indicators.note: to grab means the combined pieces take hold of the secretary, enclosing it
first means the whip comes before the party in the answer

parts.note: a strap is a leather strip used for beating
a do is an informal word for a party
a PA, personal assistant, does a secretary's work

explanation.surface: A party whip seizes a secretary to torment her, a political scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Party whip suggests the parliamentary enforcer; here the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Strappado is an old form of torture in which a victim was hoisted by the arms tied behind the back.

clue.text: "Phone or otherwise" — Michael Howard when it comes to being PM?

definitions.text: Michael Howard when it comes to being PM?

indicators.note: otherwise means the two words are put into some other order

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Tory leader will never become Prime Minister, whether he phones or not.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Howard led the Conservative Party from 2003 to 2005 and lost the 2005 election.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, Private Eye's view of Howard's prospects.

clue.text: Island shows Yeo and what he is — extremely lacking

parts.note: Tim Yeo was a Conservative MP

indicators.note: extremely lacking means the word loses its letters at both extremes

parts.note: Yeo is a Tory, a Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's island trip exposes him as one thoroughly deficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Timor is an island in the Malay Archipelago, divided between Indonesia and East Timor.

clue.text: Dismissive description of French troops on the move: "run off the premises"?

parts.note: Frog is a derogatory British slang word for a French person
soldiers moving in step march

explanation.surface: A sneer at retreating French soldiers, as if they were being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To frogmarch someone is to force them along, often out of a building, with arms held from behind.

clue.text: Poor Tone, without foreign aid, taking less in

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the reworked name surrounds the other set
poor means the four letters are in a bad, jumbled state
foreign means the three letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, left without international help, has to tighten his belt.
explanation.walkthrough: Tone is Private Eye's name for Tony Blair; 'without' is in its older sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone following a slimming diet is eating less food, so the phrase describes consuming less.

clue.text: The stuff of Oasis brother sex and drink

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex
pop is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: The Gallagher brothers' rock-star lifestyle: sex and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis were the leading band of the 1990s British guitar music movement known as Britpop.

clue.text: Specifically, www, as-jonathan-would-: say edu/cation

parts.note: the definite article is the word that points to one specific thing

indicators.note: the broadcaster Jonathan Ross cannot pronounce R and says W in its place, so his W is really an R and the swap is undone

parts.note: www is three of the letter W, written out as a number and a plural

explanation.surface: A garbled web address about how Jonathan Ross would pronounce education.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross's rhotacism earned him the nickname Wossy; reading, writing and arithmetic are traditionally the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names reading, writing and arithmetic, the traditional foundations of elementary schooling.

clue.text: Did a Fiennes, going without sex: "not right to be taken advantage of"

indicators.note: going without means the explorer's verb goes outside, wrapping round
not right means the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is a British polar explorer
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: An explorer, abstaining on an expedition, complains of being used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going without sex' reads as abstinence; it is an enclosure of the little word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to use them unfairly for your own benefit, to take advantage of them.

clue.text: Just one of many Nixon had to take out?

definitions.text: Just one of many Nixon had to take out?

parts.words: Just one of many Nixon had to take out
parts.note: read as a dinner date or a hit; in fact the published transcripts of Nixon's White House tapes cut his swearing, marking each cut in brackets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests an assassination or a dinner date; it means censored from the Watergate tapes.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive is a swear word, and Nixon's tapes famously contained many that were cut.

clue.text: Norm has runs but she kept her head

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: Someone ordinary runs about, yet a woman stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Kept her head sounds like staying calm; it is literal, as she escaped the axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr, Henry VIII's sixth wife, outlived him and so kept her head.

clue.text: Archer might have one interbreed somewhere in London

parts.note: to cross breeds is to interbreed them
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, the disgraced novelist, might have bred something in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer looks like the novelist and peer Jeffrey Archer; it is just someone shooting arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a bow weapon mounted on a stock, used by a bowman.

clue.text: Gets the better of spots

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly
second meaning: the spots on dice or dominoes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both narrowly defeats a rival and the dots marked on playing cards or dice.

clue.text: President takes issue about Southern term for "naughty bits"

indicators.note: about means the word issue is turned around, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A US President objects to a Deep South euphemism for genitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes issue' reads as objecting; issue is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussy is a vulgar slang word for the female genitals, which naughty bits coyly names.

clue.text: Master of spin "heading off entire retreat of Saddam"

parts.note: a spider spins webs

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: whole means entire

explanation.surface: A spin doctor puts out a line about Saddam pulling back entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Master of spin suggests a spin doctor or spin bowler; it is the web-spinning creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddam Hussein was captured in December 2003 hiding in a small underground pit dubbed a spider hole.

clue.text: Take into one's affections Cyclops's erection point in middle of bang

indicators.note: in a down clue, an erection raises the word upright, so it reads upwards

parts.note: Cyclops is the setter, so the setter's self is me; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: in middle of means the compass letter goes into the centre of the noise

parts.note: a boom is a loud bang
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A bawdy joke about the setter's arousal while embracing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To embosom is to clasp to the bosom, hence to take someone to your heart.

clue.text: Test produces a rather boring, singular form of diarrhoea?

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
diarrhoea is known as the runs, so one of them is a run

explanation.surface: A cricket Test produces a dull spell, likened to an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Test suggests a cricket Test match; it simply means a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or trial performed before the real thing.

clue.text: Whip gives a big wave, while holding firm

indicators.note: holding means the wave encloses the firm's letters

parts.note: a surge is a large swelling wave

explanation.surface: A party whip waves grandly while keeping a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment.

clue.text: Reportedly has the lowdown on long suffering sort, Jacko's physical 'enhancement'?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so the word for being in the know is taken by its sound

parts.note: to have the lowdown on something is to know it
Job, in the Bible, suffered patiently

explanation.surface: Gossip about Michael Jackson's cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacko was the tabloid nickname for Michael Jackson, whose rhinoplasty was much discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty is cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, Jackson's much-mocked enhancement.

clue.text: Prince: "there's catch about one taking wife"

indicators.note: about means the verb for catching goes round the pair

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: taking means one takes the wife alongside it

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A prince is caught out with a married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim prince or ruler in India.

clue.text: Brand covers bum product (extra large)

indicators.note: covers means the comedian's first name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Jo Brand is a British comedian, so her first name stands in for her surname

indicators.note: a product is something worked up, so the word bum is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A brand of extra-large bottom cream, the kind of joke Private Eye relishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand looks like a trade name; it is the comedian Jo Brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo, from the famous elephant, means very large or outsize.

clue.text: Place underground has to contend with what John Humphrys and to, do

definitions.text: what John Humphrys and to, do

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: A burial ground is overrun by Radio 4's combative interrogator.
explanation.walkthrough: John Humphrys presented Radio 4's Today programme; 'to, do' appears to be a mangled Today.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrys was famous for his tough questioning of politicians on air.

clue.text: Chucks one off the flight for "boisterous birthday celebrations"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an airline that overbooks ... a passenger off a flight
second meaning: the British custom of lifting someone up and down once per year of age

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an airline's ejection of a booked passenger and a rough schoolyard birthday ritual.

clue.text: State of US misspelled by Quayle

indicators.note: misspelled means the two letters are set in the wrong order

parts.note: Dan Quayle was US Vice-President, famous for misspelling potato

explanation.surface: Dan Quayle, notorious for a spelling gaffe, mangles an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like an American state; it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is an African country, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Space for Moore to back conclusion of editorial and grovel internally

indicators.note: internally means these pieces are placed inside the reversed name
to back means the name is read backwards
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the conclusion of editorial is its final letter
to bow is to bend low in deference

explanation.surface: An editor makes room for Patrick Moore while grovelling to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Moore suggests the astronomer Patrick Moore and space his subject; it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move or work freely.
